gloss: to be absorbed in; to spend one's days doing

definitions.gloss: to be absorbed in, to spend one's days doing, to be occupied with day and night
definitions.explanation: To devote oneself to a single activity from morning to night, day after day. Implies that the person does almost nothing else. Often used with に to mark the activity.

examples.japanese: {勉強|べんきょう}に{明|あ}け{暮|く}れる。
examples.english: To be absorbed in studying day and night.

examples.japanese: {試験|しけん}{前|まえ}は{毎日|まいにち}{勉強|べんきょう}に{明|あ}け{暮|く}れていた。
examples.english: Before the exam, I spent every day absorbed in studying.

examples.japanese: {若|わか}いころは{仕事|しごと}に{明|あ}け{暮|く}れ、{家族|かぞく}との{時間|じかん}がほとんどなかった。
examples.english: In my younger days, I was consumed by work and had almost no time with my family.

notes:
CONJUGATION:
Ichidan verb ({一段動詞|いちだんどうし}).
- Negative: {明|あ}け{暮|く}れない
- Polite: {明|あ}け{暮|く}れます
- Te-form: {明|あ}け{暮|く}れて
- Past: {明|あ}け{暮|く}れた

PATTERN:
〜に{明|あ}け{暮|く}れる: to be absorbed in ~
The activity is marked with に.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {仕事|しごと}に{明|あ}け{暮|く}れる: to be consumed by work
- {勉強|べんきょう}に{明|あ}け{暮|く}れる: to be absorbed in studying
- {練習|れんしゅう}に{明|あ}け{暮|く}れる: to devote oneself to practice

ETYMOLOGY:
{明|あ}ける (to dawn) + {暮|く}れる (to grow dark) — from dawn to dusk, the idea is that one spends the entire day, from sunrise to sunset, engaged in the activity.
